title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from Black Grapes and Their Places
objectives: Link each grape to its classic regions
Explain how climate and soil shape each

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its classic region.
steps.explanation: Each grape has a benchmark place.

steps.prompt: Which grape is pale in colour yet very tannic?
steps.explanation: Nebbiolo has few stable pigments but lots of tannin and acidity.

steps.prompt: Which grapes are part of a classic GSM blend?
steps.explanation: GSM stands for Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre.

steps.prompt: Merlot ripens earlier than Cabernet Sauvignon.
steps.explanation: Yes. That's why Merlot suits the cooler clay of the Right Bank.

steps.prompt: In Spain's Ribera del Duero, Tempranillo is called Tinto ____.
steps.explanation: Tinto Fino is the local name. Tinta Roriz is the Douro's name, and Tinto Cão is a different Portuguese grape.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cabernet and Merlot shape Bordeaux's two banks
Pinot Noir and Nebbiolo need special sites and time
Syrah, Grenache, Tempranillo and Sangiovese lead their regions
Malbec, Zinfandel, Pinotage and Carmenère define New World countries
